newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto, husband have a laugh.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto, husband have a laugh.

text.p: Benazir Bhutto said on Monday she had shared a laugh with her detained husband when she visited him in an ad hoc jail near Pakistan's capital.
The ousted prime minister said that on Sunday she paid her second visit to Asif Ali Zardari since he was detained without charges and confined to an official guest house near Islamabad.

"We were both having a laugh about it because we said that even when (then president) Ghulam Ishaq Khan got rid of governments, he never used this without charges," Bhutto told Reuters Television in an interview at the prime minister's official residence.
Khan sacked Bhutto's first government in August 1990, citing massive abuses of power and corruption. She was later cleared of eight counts of misrule, and recaptured power in 1993.
Khan also dismissed former prime minister Nawaz Sharif in 1993. He was later re-instated by a court order.
Bhutto said her husband was free for six weeks after her dismissal in 1990 before he was arrested on 12 charges of corruption, kept behind bars for two years and then freed.

"We were both laughing, and I was saying that I was (held) on many occasions during martial law, but now it has to be my spouse that has to face the same charge under the presidential, civilian equivalent of martial law," she said.
Bhutto was referring to her detention during martial law under General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq, who toppled her father, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, in 1977.
She said her husband's morale was very high and that he had foreseen his plight.
"He would always joke and tell people here, 'I'm the one who will have to go to jail when the government goes, and none of you listened to me'," she said.
Recently Zardari flew to Britain for tests following an eye operation. Doctors had wanted him to stay in England, she said, but he returned at her urging.
"I said, 'Darling, the nation awaits you'," Bhutto explained.
